annotationRationale: The integer prices force a common multiple of the four quantities. Prime factorization finds its minimum, and total price divided by unit price gives the candy count.
sourceMethod: Follows the official least-common-multiple argument, including checking that 420 cents produces valid integer prices for the other colors.

review.mathCheck: The total must be divisible by 12, 14, 15, and 20. Their LCM is 420, so the minimum count is 420/20=21, choice B. Prices 35, 30, and 28 cents establish attainability.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA AMC 10B solution 7, page 4. It retains the common-total LCM method and feasibility check, explicitly explaining the greatest-prime-power rule.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed LCM node and supporting prime-factorization and price-quantity nodes fit the worked method. Minimality and feasibility are both established.
